title: US Bank Reserves Rise, Surpassing $3 Trillion
content: U.S. bank reserves rose by approximately $54 billion to $3.034 trillion by the week ending October 8, 2025, marking the first increase in nine weeks and surpassing the $3 trillion threshold for the first time since July 2020. This rise follows an eight-week decline, the longest such period since July 2020, which was driven by increased U.S. Treasury debt issuance to rebuild cash balances after the debt ceiling was raised in July. That issuance drained liquidity from Federal Reserve liabilities, including the overnight reverse repurchase (RRP) agreements and bank reserves. The recent uptick in reserves is attributed to the RRP facility nearing depletion, which halted the prior downward trend. The data, released by the Federal Reserve, is being monitored by the Federal Reserve as it evaluates further balance sheet reductions. title: U.S. Federal Reserve

title: La FED recortó la tasa de referencia hasta 4% - Bank Magazine
content: On September 17 2025 the U.S. Federal Reserve released its quarterly projections. It raised its 2025 GDP growth forecast from 1.4 % to 1.6 % and left the unemployment rate unchanged at 4.5 %. Inflation expectations remained unchanged: the PCE price index is projected at 3.0 % YoY and core PCE at 3.1 %. The Fed’s FOMC members signaled two additional 0.25‑percentage‑point cuts in 2025, which would bring the federal funds rate to a 3.50 %–3.75 % range by year‑end, an advance of the cuts that had previously been scheduled for 2026. For 2026 the Fed projects 1.8 % growth, unemployment 4.4 %–4.5 %, and inflation near 2.6 % for both PCE and core. In 2027 it expects another rate cut, higher growth, lower unemployment and lower inflation. Interest‑rate futures confirm at least two cuts before year‑end, aligning with the FOMC’s official projections.
